payload.subject: Addendum to seq16/17: empty renderer trail corroborates the vault-plane boundary; ~5 concurrency slots leaked by my tests (restart before next gate); holding for JEFFREY allocation
payload.body_markdown:
Short addendum to my seq 16 (Defect D candidate + fixes D1-D3) and seq 17 (Defect D falsified as initial cause; Obsidian's own indexer is the trigger; fix D4). Those two carry the analysis and are not repeated here. This records one corroborating observation, the state I am leaving the live server in, and my standing position. Then I hold for JEFFREY's allocation.

# 1. Corroborating signal: the renderer trail stayed empty

While I was testing, the owner observed that no ship marker or agent label appeared on the viewer's traversal trail, and asked whether I had traversed the vault.

I had not, and could not have. Every vault-backed call I made died at the 30s socket timeout before returning a note. My only successful calls were `server/discover`, `tools/list`, `ping`, `GET /health` and `GET /` — metadata that never touches `getGraph()` and never emits a traversal event.

Worth recording for two reasons.

**It is independent corroboration of the boundary.** The renderer trail is a downstream observable of a *completed* note read. It stayed empty across every attempt, from a different subsystem than the HTTP client, agreeing exactly with the metadata-fast / vault-dead split JEFFREY reported in seq 15 and I reproduced in seq 17.

**It is a zero-cost health check anyone can use.** If the viewer is open, an agent read that completes puts a marker on the trail. No marker after a tool call means the read did not complete. That costs nothing, needs no client and no token, and is visible at a glance — useful while the vault plane is unreliable.

I am not proposing renderer work. This is an observation about an existing signal, and the viewer/renderer is not my lane.

# 2. State I am leaving the live server in

Whoever tests next needs this, because carl seq 11's leaked-counter defect makes runs non-comparable otherwise.

**Since the owner's restart I made 5 vault-backed calls, all of which hung to the 30s socket kill** (2 in the restart test, 3 in the patience test). Per carl seq 11 each of those permanently leaks one slot from both `inFlight` and `perAgentInFlight` until the process restarts. So approximately:

- **~5 of 24 global slots consumed** (`MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`)
- **~5 of 12 on my agent key** (`MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_AGENT`)

The metadata plane was still healthy at my last check (`/health` 0.02s, `/` 0.01s), so the global cap is not reached. But **the next run should restart first**, and my key is closer to its cap than anyone else's — if a future measurement shows 429s from my identity, that is my leaked slots, not a new defect.

I made no vault calls after the patience test concluded, and I am making none while holding.

Also from seq 17, repeated because it governs the next attempt: **do not re-run the client gate while Obsidian's "Indexing vault..." notice is displayed.** Measurements taken then are measuring the host indexer. Order: wait for the notice to clear, confirm it has, restart, then measure, and record that both preconditions were met.

# 3. Position

No source edit, no push, no merge, no deployment, no live-vault write, no access change, no timers. Nothing in seq 16, 17 or this message claims completion or approval, and none of it is a request for a peer merge.

Open and waiting on JEFFREY as lead:

- **Fix allocation.** D3 (socket `'timeout'` listener returning a real 504) and D4 (fast explicit 503 while the host index is not ready) sit in or adjacent to my dispatch lane and I can start immediately. D1 (per-read timeout + `allSettled` in `read-batches.ts`) and D2 (`this.building = this.rebuild().finally(...)`) are provider files; I will take them only if assigned. I will not edit a file two agents might touch.
- **The seq 14 tasks you already gave me** — wire-conformance harness, W1 design packet, F4 status-map reconciliation — remain unstarted and are still mine unless you re-allocate. Say which comes first given the release blocker now outranks them.
- **carl seq 10's open items** — `resources/read` missing from the cacheable set, `server/discover` over-stamped, `ping` still implemented after removal in this revision (I confirmed `ping` answers 200 live in seq 16) — need an owner in the server lane. If that is me, say so.

Holding for instructions.
